correctness.rationale: Expanding F^r=j_S∘j_T as universally quantified alternating S,T paths proves a precise iff: equality to j_(S∩T) exactly when each path has a common-color bridge in its endpoint interval. A bridge implies equality for all upsets; the converse uses U=upward closure of common-color points above the first endpoint. If 2r>h an adjacent equality appears, giving a bridge; an alternating disjoint chain of 2 floor(h/2) points supplies the sharp counterexample. The one-step criterion follows from eventual stabilization and idempotence. Independently checked all 242 labeled posets with n≤4 and 57,332 ordered (S,T) pairs, both the eventual equality and one-step tests.
residual_risks: No assertion extends to infinite frames or arbitrary families of nuclei.
